quiz.question: How does the luma library handle drawing on an OLED display?

answers.answer: It sends each drawing command directly to the display one at a time
It composes the full frame in an in-memory image, then flushes it to the screen
It writes pixels to the display as soon as each draw call is made
It stores the frame on an SD card and loads it to the display

quiz.explanation: The luma library uses a framebuffer approach: everything is drawn to an in-memory image first, then the complete frame is sent to the display when the 'with canvas(device)' block ends.

quiz.question: What happens when the 'with canvas(device)' block ends?

answers.answer: The display is cleared and powered off
The composed image is flushed to the screen
The program pauses until the next frame is requested

quiz.explanation: The 'with canvas(device)' block acts as a framebuffer boundary. When it ends, the fully composed in-memory image gets pushed to the display in one batch.

quiz.question: Which of the following can you draw on a pixel-based OLED display?

answers.answer: Only text characters from the built-in font
Only geometric shapes like lines and rectangles
Text at any size, shapes, lines, and rectangles
Only bitmap images loaded from files

quiz.explanation: On a pixel display, you control every dot. You can render text at any size using a chosen font, and draw shapes like lines, rectangles, and circles using the same drawing library.
